title: OAuth 2.0 OIDC flows scopes PKCE and token storage
concepts: OAuth 2.0 is an authorization framework: a client obtains bounded access to a resource server through an authorization server. OpenID Connect adds an authentication layer and ID token for the client.
Authorization Code with PKCE is the preferred flow for public browser and native clients. The client sends a code challenge and proves possession of its verifier when redeeming the code.
Redirect URI exactness, state, nonce, issuer, audience, and token storage defend different protocol boundaries and must be checked by the receiving client or server.
OAuth is not a synonym for login. RFC 9700 is the current OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice; OAuth 2.1 must not be described as finalized unless its standards status is verified.

inventory.title: Authorization Code, PKCE, browser/native clients, and security boundaries
items: OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice RFC 9700
RFC 9700 updates RFCs 6749, 6750, and 6819 and consolidates current OAuth 2.0 security recommendations; it does not change OAuth into an authentication protocol.

OAuth 2.1 is not presented as a finalized standard.
Token validation and browser session storage details are covered in t05-003.
